correctness.rationale: The exact band inequality of arXiv:2012.14344v1 yields, after normalization, the leading trigonometric polynomial \(\cos(2k(\pi-L_3))-\cos(2\pi k)=2\sin(kL_2)\sin(kL_3)\) with a uniform \(O(k^{-2})\) remainder. On rational ratios the leading zeros have multiplicity at most two, so the energy-weighted disagreement set has \(o(K)\) measure. The period average is then computed exactly by square-wave Fourier correlation, giving correlation \(0\) if either reduced integer is even and \(1/(pq)\) if both are odd. Flat bands are measure zero. The bundled exact rational replay agrees for all coprime \(p,q\le25\), while numerical checks of the exact inequality agree with the predicted limits.

evidence: The 2020 source gives the exact inequality and leading product \(\sin(kL_2)\sin(kL_3)\) but infers independence of the two signs for every asymmetric chain.
The 2024 source invokes torus filling for incommensurate arcs and then asserts that the same area fraction holds for rational unequal arcs without computing the closed rational orbit average.
The present proof computes that closed orbit average and shows that it differs from the torus area exactly in the reduced odd-odd case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim is not a corollary of the published statements; it corrects their implication on a specific nongeneric locus. The exact source equation supplies premises, but the parity-sensitive orbit average is an additional argument.

originality.rationale: The 2020/2022 primary paper states density \(1/2\) for every asymmetric collapsed-link chain; the 2024 interpolation paper repeats the statement and explicitly extends it to unequal rationally related arcs. The present odd-odd rational correction is therefore not implied by those sources. Generic-edge universality does not cover rational commensurability. Targeted bibliographic and full-text searches found no equivalent correction or erratum.
residual_risks: An equivalent correction may exist in an unindexed note, comment, thesis, or source using unrelated terminology.
The finding is a correction on a nongeneric rational locus; it does not classify finite-cutoff oscillations or small positive connecting lengths.

value.rationale: The claim corrects a published transport-density statement on an infinite arithmetic family. It separates generic/incommensurate and even-odd commensurate ratios from odd-odd commensurate ratios, gives explicit exact densities, and produces the concrete ratio \(1/3\) with density \(2/3\). This is structurally relevant because the cited papers use the density as a high-energy conductivity descriptor; the result is not a renaming, arbitrary slice, or table recomputation.
